subject: Agriculture
title: Watermills and Windmills
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Watermills and Windmills.

hook.text: Grinding grain by hand takes hours. A watermill does the same work in minutes, powered by a stream.

buildup.text: Romans built watermills, but medieval Europe perfected them. England's Domesday Book lists over 6,000 mills.

discovery.text: Windmills appeared around 1100 CE in areas without reliable streams—flat, windy places like the Netherlands.

twist.text: Lords controlled the mills and charged fees. Peasants were often forced to use the lord's mill by law.

climax.text: Mills were medieval Europe's first industrial machines—a quiet revolution in energy and food processing.

punchline.text: Water and wind freed human hands—but filled lordly pockets.

quiz.question: How many watermills were recorded in England's Domesday Book?
